reproduction.conclusion: The failed smoke used an interpreter whose torch build has NO CUDA (the bare system Python 3.11), not the project venv.

pyvenv_cfg.note: The project venv is created from the system Python 3.11 but isolates site-packages, so the venv has torch 2.6.0+cu124 while the system base has torch 2.10.0+cpu.

root_cause_explanation: The canonical smoke must run under the project venv D:/Softfors/jup/.venv/Scripts/python.exe (torch 2.6.0+cu124). At smoke time the process resolved torch 2.10.0+cpu (CPU-only build, torch.version.cuda=None), so torch.cuda.is_available() returned False and src.utils.device.get_device(require_cuda=True) raised CudaUnavailableError before any canonical model construction. This is an INTERPRETER/BUILD selection defect (B), triggered by invoking the bare system Python 3.11 instead of the venv (E). The GPU, driver, and the venv itself are healthy.
